text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Denmark is isolated in its demands for tighter environmental stipulations in the European Union reforms to be agreed at this week's EU Amsterdam summit, with only Sweden supporting prime minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen's calls for tougher guarantees.

--After the EU Summit in Amsterdam, Danish prime minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen is expected to call a new national referendum in Denmark on reforms to the existing Maastricht treaty. The vote is expected to be held in January or February 1998.

--Growing world trade and rising international competition mean that Denmark and other western nations are entering a period with historically low price increases, meaning that the risk of a return of high inflation has drastically declined, according to an economic report produced by Unidanmark, the second biggest Danish bank.

--Third biggest Danish bank BG Bank is ripe for a merger or takeover by foreign banking interests after the recent collapse of its cooperation pact with leading local mortgage firm Nykredit, experts say.

--1996 was a record year for Danish advertising agencies with television commercials taking a bigger share of the cake at the cost of newspaper advertising. Of a total of 19.381 billion crowns spent on advertising in Denmark in 1996, 8.5 billion went to media.
